Beta diversity of microbes on diferent frog skins

Roger Calvas

2026-11-16

Goals

  1. Load in phyloseq data.
  2. Evaluate sequencing depth and remove samples, if needed.
  3. Normalize the read counts between samples.
  4. Calculate community dissimilarities. Numbers between 0 and 1. If 0, completely similar versus if they are 1, then they’re completely dissimilar.
    1. Sorensen: Shared Species as a binary value: Abundance-unweighted
    2. Bray-Curtis: Shared Abundant species: Abundance-weighted
  5. Run statistics with functions from the vegan R package:
    1. PERMANOVA with adonis2().
    2. betadispR with betadisper() and permutest().
  6. Visualize the community data with two unconstrained Ordinations:
    1. PCoA: Linear Method. Eigenvalue = how much variation is explained by each axis. Choose to view axis 1, 2, 3, etc. and plot them together.
    2. NMDS: Non-linear. Smush multiple Dimensions into 2 or 3 axes. Need to report Stress value (ideally <0.15).

Inputs

  1. We will need the clean_physeq.RData

Outputs

This is an exciting analysis!!! We get to answer another one of our scientific questions!

  1. Calculated beta-diversity dissimilarity measures (e.g. Sorensen, Bray-Curtis, abundance-unweighted and -weighted UniFrac) across every sample.
  2. Ordination figures (i.e., PCoA/NMDS) to include in the scientific paper that visualize the data as it relates to the scientific question.
  3. Statistical tests (i.e., PERMANOVA & betadisper) conveying the measured and quantified changes and patterns in biodiversity.

Scientific Question

Se relaciona la localidad con la diversidad de la piel de las diferentes especies de rana que lo habitan?

  • Null Hypothesis: La localidad no se relaciona directamente con la diversidad de la piel de las ranas
  • Alternative Hypothesis: La diversidad cambia con relacion directa a la localidad

Set up

Timing of this script

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Set the seed

set.seed(3980)

Load Packages, colors & functions

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, phyloseq, patchwork, vegan, 
               install = FALSE)

# Load Colors 
source("code/colors.R")

# Load functions 
source("code/functions.R")

Load in the data

# load phyloseq object
load("data/its/03_PreProcessing/clean_physeq.RData")
clean_physeq
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 3033 taxa and 34 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 34 samples by 89 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 3033 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
# Intuition check on seq depth
min(sample_sums(clean_physeq))
## [1] 14002

Normalizar conteos

Explore the Raw Read Counts

# calculate read counts per sample 
raw_TotalSeqs_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  # Calculate the total number of sequences/reads
  sample_sums() %>%
  data.frame()

# Take a look 
head(raw_TotalSeqs_df)
##             .
## ANF-004 52145
## ANF-006 66935
## ANF-007 38988
## ANF-011 51603
## ANF-018 47765
## ANF-021 54641
# Rename the column 
colnames(raw_TotalSeqs_df)[1] <- "TotalSeqs"

# add a new column of num_ASVs (RAW, non-noramlized # ASVs)
raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df <- 
  raw_TotalSeqs_df %>%
  mutate(num_ASVs = colSums(otu_table(clean_physeq) > 1))

#View(raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df)

# Plot histogram of seq depth 
rawSeq_histogram <- 
  raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = TotalSeqs)) + 
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)  + 
  labs(title = "Raw Seq Depth Histogram",
       x = "Total sequences",
       y = "Number of samples") + 
  theme_bw()

# Plot Seq Depth versus num_ASVs
rawSeq_vs_numASV_plot <- 
  raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_ASVs, y = TotalSeqs)) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  labs(title = "Seq Depth vs # ASVs",
       x = "Total ASVs per sample",
       y = "Total seqs per sample") + 
  theme_bw()

# is it significant? 
summary(lm(TotalSeqs ~ num_ASVs, data = raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df))
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = TotalSeqs ~ num_ASVs, data = raw_TotalSeqsASVs_df)

rawSeq_histogram + rawSeq_vs_numASV_plot +

Scale Read Counts

min(sample_sums(clean_physeq))
## [1] 14002
# Scale the reads
scaled_physeq <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  scale_reads(round = "matround")  

# Look at it 
scaled_physeq
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 3030 taxa and 34 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 34 samples by 89 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 3030 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
# Save it
save(scaled_physeq, file ="data/its/05_Ordination/scaled_physeq.RData")

# Look at it more!
#View(data.frame(otu_table(clean_physeq)))
#View(data.frame(otu_table(scaled_physeq)))

# Confirm seq read depth of scaled_physeq 
scaled_TotalSeqs_df <- 
  scaled_physeq %>%
  sample_sums() %>%
  data.frame()

colnames(scaled_TotalSeqs_df)[1] <- "TotalSeqs"

# add a new column of num_ASVs (RAW, non-noramlized # ASVs)
scaled_TotalSeqsASVs_df <- 
  scaled_TotalSeqs_df %>%
  mutate(num_ASVs = colSums(otu_table(scaled_physeq) > 1))

# Plot it! 
scaledSeq_histogram <- 
  scaled_TotalSeqs_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = TotalSeqs)) + 
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) + 
  labs(title = "Scaled Seq Depth Histogram")+ 
  theme_bw()

# Scaling always gives us a range! 
range(scaled_TotalSeqs_df$TotalSeqs)
## [1] 13998 14014
# Set the axis min and max for the next plot 
max_y <- max(scaled_TotalSeqs_df$TotalSeqs) + 10
min_y <- min(scaled_TotalSeqs_df$TotalSeqs) - 10 

# Now, draw the plot 
scaledSeq_vs_numASV_plot <- 
  scaled_TotalSeqsASVs_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_ASVs, y = TotalSeqs)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(min_y, max_y)) +
  #geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Scaled: Seq Depth vs # ASVs")

# Put the two plots together.
scaledSeq_histogram + scaledSeq_vs_numASV_plot +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

Create metadata after pruning

# Create Metadata_df after the prune
metadata_df <- 
  scaled_physeq %>%
  sample_data() %>%
  data.frame()

Permanovas for bray curtis

# bray
## 1. Run with by = terms for R² values, sensitive to order of variables! 
##   
bray_status_adonis_terms1 <- adonis2(scaled_Bray_dist ~ localidad + posicion_vertical_cm, data = metadata_df, by = "terms")
bray_status_adonis_terms1
## Permutation test for adonis under reduced model
## Terms added sequentially (first to last)
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## adonis2(formula = scaled_Bray_dist ~ localidad + posicion_vertical_cm, data = metadata_df, by = "terms")
##                      Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)    
## localidad             4   2.1871 0.13867 1.1680  0.001 ***
## posicion_vertical_cm  1   0.4774 0.03027 1.0198  0.350    
## Residual             28  13.1076 0.83106                  
## Total                33  15.7721 1.00000                  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Check the order of the terms
bray_status_adonis_terms2 <- adonis2(scaled_Bray_dist ~ posicion_vertical_cm + localidad, data = metadata_df, by = "terms")
bray_status_adonis_terms2
## Permutation test for adonis under reduced model
## Terms added sequentially (first to last)
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## adonis2(formula = scaled_Bray_dist ~ posicion_vertical_cm + localidad, data = metadata_df, by = "terms")
##                      Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)   
## posicion_vertical_cm  1   0.4627 0.02934 0.9885  0.583   
## localidad             4   2.2018 0.13960 1.1758  0.002 **
## Residual             28  13.1076 0.83106                 
## Total                33  15.7721 1.00000                 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 2. Compara si hay interaccion entre localidad y altura juntas (by margin) 
bray_status_adonis_margin <- adonis2(scaled_Bray_dist ~ localidad * posicion_vertical_cm, data = metadata_df, by = "margin")
bray_status_adonis_margin

Permanovas for Sorensen

# sorensen
## 1. Run with by = terms for R² values, sensitive to order of variables! 
## ALWAYS check and confirm the order of your terms and how they interact with each other.  
sorensen_status_adonis_terms1 <- adonis2(scaled_sorensen_dist ~ localidad + posicion_vertical_cm, data = metadata_df, by = "terms")
sorensen_status_adonis_terms1

Betadisper: Testing Variances/Dispersions

Sorensen

# Homogeneity of Disperson test with beta dispr
# Sorensen Betadisper - status 
dispr_sorensen_localidad <- betadisper(scaled_sorensen_dist, metadata_df$localidad)
# permutest() performs a non-parametric permutation test, which is robust and valid for the kind of data used in beta diversity analysis (e.g., dissimilarity matrices).
permutest(dispr_sorensen_localidad)
## 
## Permutation test for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## Response: Distances
##           Df    Sum Sq    Mean Sq      F N.Perm Pr(>F)
## Groups     4 0.0005451 0.00013627 0.3911    999  0.809
## Residuals 29 0.0101039 0.00034841
# Homogeneidad de dispersión para Bray-Curtis por localidad
  dispr_bray_localidad <- betadisper(scaled_Bray_dist, metadata_df$localidad)
permutest(dispr_bray_localidad)
## 
## Permutation test for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions
## Permutation: free
## Number of permutations: 999
## 
## Response: Distances
##           Df    Sum Sq    Mean Sq      F N.Perm Pr(>F)

PCoA: Principal Coordinate analysis

### SORENSEN 
# First, calculate PCoA with Soresen
scaled_soren_pcoa <- 
  ordinate(physeq = scaled_physeq,
         method = "PCoA",
         distance = "bray", binary = TRUE)

# Take a quick look
str(scaled_soren_pcoa)
## List of 5
##  $ correction: chr [1:2] "none" "1"
##  $ note      : chr "There were no negative eigenvalues. No correction was applied"
##  $ values    :'data.frame':  33 obs. of  5 variables:
##   ..$ Eigenvalues   : num [1:33] 0.719 0.67 0.637 0.607 0.582 ...
##   ..$ Relative_eig  : num [1:33] 0.0465 0.0434 0.0412 0.0393 0.0377 ...
##   ..$ Broken_stick  : num [1:33] 0.1239 0.0936 0.0784 0.0683 0.0608 ...
##   ..$ Cumul_eig     : num [1:33] 0.0465 0.0899 0.1312 0.1705 0.2082 ...
##   ..$ Cumul_br_stick: num [1:33] 0.124 0.218 0.296 0.364 0.425 ...
##  $ vectors   : num [1:34, 1:33] -0.1967 -0.0718 -0.1595 -0.2833 -0.1661 ...
##   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
##   .. ..$ : chr [1:34] "ANF-004" "ANF-006" "ANF-007" "ANF-011" ...
##   .. ..$ : chr [1:33] "Axis.1" "Axis.2" "Axis.3" "Axis.4" ...
##  $ trace     : num 15.4
##  - attr(*, "class")= chr "pcoa"
# Plot it
sorensen_pcoa_plot <-
      plot_ordination(physeq = scaled_physeq,
                      ordination = scaled_soren_pcoa,
                      color = "localidad",
                      title = "Sorensen PCoA") +
      geom_point(aes(size = posicion_vertical_cm, color = localidad), alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_color_manual(values = localidad_colors, name = "Localidad") +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "Altura (cm)", range = c(2, 6)) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position = "right")

### BRAY-CURTIS PCoA
scaled_bray_pcoa <-
  ordinate(physeq = scaled_physeq,
           method = "PCoA",
           distance = "bray", binary = FALSE)
# Plot it
bray_pcoa_plot <-
  plot_ordination(physeq = scaled_physeq,
                  ordination = scaled_bray_pcoa,
                  color = "localidad",
                  title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA") +
  geom_point(aes(size = posicion_vertical_cm, color = localidad), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = localidad_colors, name = "Localidad") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Altura (cm)", range = c(2, 6)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Mostrar ambos PCoA juntos
sorensen_pcoa_plot + bray_pcoa_plot +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
